name: Quote junk removal jobs from texted photos with Twilio, OpenAI, Google Sheets and Google Calendar

parameters.text: These photos were texted to a junk removal company by a customer who wants the things in them hauled away. In plain text under 200 words: 1) list every item that would be hauled, with a count, grouped sensibly (for example '2 mattresses, 1 dresser, about 12 bags of trash'); 2) estimate the whole pile as a fraction of a 15 cubic yard box truck (about an eighth, a quarter, half, three quarters, full, or more than one load); 3) say if it is mostly heavy material like dirt, concrete, brick or shingles; 4) flag anything a hauler normally cannot take (paint, chemicals, propane, asbestos, medical waste); 5) say if the photos overlap (the same pile from different angles) so nothing is counted twice; 6) note access problems you can see (stairs, narrow gate, upstairs). If a photo is not of junk, say so.

messageValues.message: You price junk removal jobs for a small hauling company. Match what was seen to the company's own price list and never invent prices.

parameters.content:
## Photo quotes for junk removal and hauling

Most junk removal quotes start with a customer texting a few photos of a pile. Pricing them by eye, one at a time, is where evenings go. This turns the photos into a priced text in about a minute, using your own price list, and only pulls you in when the job is big or odd.

### How it works
1. A customer texts photos to your Twilio number. Each photo is fetched from Twilio and saved to Google Drive.
2. OpenAI describes what is in the pile, how much of a truck it fills, anything heavy, and anything you do not take.
3. A second AI step matches that to the Price list tab in your spreadsheet. The total is added up in code from your prices, never guessed by the model.
4. Quotes under your limit go straight to the customer. Anything over the limit, unclear, heavy or unwanted comes to your phone: reply YES, a new price, or NO.
5. The customer replies YES and a day. A hold lands on your Google Calendar and both of you get a confirmation.
6. Every half hour it reminds you about quotes waiting on you, nudges a quiet customer once, and expires old quotes.

### Setup steps
1. Add Twilio, OpenAI, Google Sheets, Google Drive and Google Calendar credentials.
2. Run Create my spreadsheet once, fix the prices on the Price list tab, and paste the spreadsheet ID, your Twilio number, your mobile and your calendar's address into Your settings. For your main calendar that is your Google account email.
3. In Twilio, point the number's "A message comes in" webhook at this workflow's Text comes in URL.
4. Publish, then text a photo to the number yourself.

### Try it first
Text two photos of a chair to your own Twilio number. Then reply YES Saturday. For the approval path, send a big pile and answer the text that reaches your mobile with YES, NO or a price.

### 1. Three ways in
A text to your Twilio number, the half-hourly check and the one-time setup. Twilio is answered at once, then the text is sorted: your reply, or a customer's photos, YES or question.

### 2. Your decision by text
YES sends the quote, a number sends it at your price, NO passes. The customer and you both get a text.

### 3. Photos become a price
Each photo is fetched from Twilio and kept in Drive. OpenAI describes the pile, then matches it to your Price list tab. The total is added up in code. Big, unclear or unwanted loads wait for your OK; the rest go straight out.

### 4. YES books it
The day in the reply (Saturday, tomorrow afternoon, 2pm) becomes a hold on your Google Calendar. No day means the next business day.

### 5. Everything else
A first text with no photos is asked for some. An address is saved. A real question is passed to you instead of answered by a bot.

### 6. Half-hourly follow-up
Reminds you about quotes waiting on you, nudges a quiet customer once in daytime hours, and expires old quotes.

### 7. One-time setup
Run Create my spreadsheet once for the Quotes and Price list tabs, then fix the example prices.
